title: EPIC: Provable source compatibility with OpenVMS
description:
Goal: Demonstrate that real OpenVMS C programs — written by VMS developers, not by us — compile against OVMX headers and run correctly on Linux.

"Source compatible" means: a VMS C program that compiles with DEC C / VSI C on OpenVMS Alpha/x86-64 also compiles with gcc/clang against OVMX headers and produces correct results.

Proof ladder (each milestone proves a wider slice):
1. Eight-Cubed single-file examples (sys$ + lib$ surface)
2. Eight-Cubed multi-file utilities (real programs)
3. MMK (CLI$, lib$tparse, lib$find_file — real build tool)
4. NETLIB + MX or WASD subset (QIO + AST + networking — real server)

This epic replaces the old Phase 8-10 monoliths with a dependency-wired, corpus-driven path. Each milestone is proven by compiling real VMS code, not hand-written tests.

title: Define source compatibility contract
description:
Deliverable: docs/compatibility-contract.md

Define what "source compatible with OpenVMS" means concretely:

1. **Target platform**: OpenVMS Alpha C (DEC C) — the most widely available source base. Not VAX, not Itanium-only.

2. **API surface**: Enumerate every sys$, lib$, str$, mth$, ots$ function OVMX implements. Map against OpenVMS Alpha documentation. Categorize as: implemented, stubbed, not-yet-implemented.

3. **Header fidelity**: List every public header OVMX provides (starlet.h, descrip.h, ssdef.h, etc.). For each, state whether struct layouts match OpenVMS Alpha (size, alignment, field order).

4. **Status code contract**: VMS status codes (odd=success, even=error) — list all SS$_ codes implemented in ssdef.h vs OpenVMS.

5. **What is NOT in scope**: Binary compatibility, VAX/Itanium-only APIs, privileged kernel APIs, cluster services, DECwindows/Motif.

6. **Compatibility tiers**:
   - Tier 1 (must work): Core sys$ services, descriptors, status codes, RMS sequential I/O, logical names, process management, condition handling
   - Tier 2 (should work): RMS indexed, CLI$, lib$tparse, formatted output, event flags + ASTs
   - Tier 3 (stretch): QIO networking, MAIL$, advanced RMS, DECC$ features

This contract becomes the acceptance criteria for every downstream milestone.
notes:
Agent actively working: reading all OVMX headers (starlet.h, descrip.h, ssdef.h, RTL files, prvdef.h, libclidef.h, DCL builtins). Building full API inventory for compatibility-contract.md. ~40 tools used, deep into header audit.
Session pause: agent completed full API audit of all headers. Now writing docs/compatibility-contract.md. Will complete in background.
close_reason: docs/compatibility-contract.md written (683 lines). Full API audit: 53 sys$ services, complete lib$/str$/mth$ RTL, 4 ots$ routines, 75 SSextglob codes, 50+ RMSextglob codes, 24 DCL builtins. Two struct divergences documented (item_list_3 pointer size, FAB/RAB extended fields). Three compatibility tiers mapped to three validation milestones. lib$tparse flagged as key blocking stub.

title: Build corpus-driven conformance harness
description:
Deliverable: tests/conformance/ harness that compiles and runs real VMS corpus programs against OVMX headers automatically.

Extends the existing run_conformance.sh (which runs 8 hand-written tests) to handle real VMS source code from the corpus.

Requirements:
1. **Compile each corpus program** against OVMX headers with gcc. Capture compiler output (errors, warnings).
2. **Categorize results**: compile-pass, compile-fail (with missing symbol/header), link-fail, run-pass, run-fail, run-crash.
3. **Machine-readable output**: JSON report with per-program status, missing APIs, missing headers.
4. **Gap extraction**: From compile errors, automatically extract lists of missing sys$/lib$/str$ functions, missing headers, missing constants.
5. **CI integration**: Runs in GitHub Actions. The pass rate is the project metric.
6. **Regression detection**: If a previously-passing program stops compiling, that is a CI failure.

The harness drives all downstream work — every compile error becomes a bead, every fix is verified by the harness.

Process:
1. Run harness against tier1-examples corpus
2. Triage failures: group by missing API/header/constant
3. Create child beads for each gap category (e.g., "implement sys$filescan", "add JPI$_ constants to jpidef.h")

5. Milestone is done when pass rate reaches 80%+

The remaining 20% may require APIs we intentionally defer (privileged ops, cluster services, etc.) — those get documented in the compatibility contract as Tier 3 / out-of-scope.

This milestone proves: core sys$ services, descriptors, status codes, lib$ RTL, str$ RTL, basic RMS, logical names, process info, condition handling all work with real VMS code.

title: CRTL shim + header binary compatibility audit
description:
Deliverable: VMS C Runtime Library shim (libvmscrtl) + verified struct layout compatibility with OpenVMS Alpha.

This is the current vms-iuu bead (Phase 9), reprioritized from P4 to P1 and placed in the dependency chain.

Two sub-deliverables:

**1. CRTL Shim (src/vmscrtl/)**
- Intercepts stdio calls to route through VMS logical name translation + RMS
- fopen("SYS$LOGIN:DATA.TXT", "r") translates logicals, parses VMS filespecs
- fopen("file.dat", "r", "rfm=var", "rat=cr") — VMS optional RMS arguments
- NOT a libc replacement — thin interception layer above glibc
- DECC$ feature switches (DECC$FILENAME_UNIX_ONLY, DECC$EFS_CHARSET, etc.)
- vaxc$errno alongside errno

**2. Header Binary Compatibility Audit**
- Compare OVMX structs against real OpenVMS Alpha headers
- Critical structs: dsc$descriptor_s, FAB, RAB, NAM, item_list_3
- Any padding, field ordering, or size differences cause silent data corruption
- FAB has internal OVMX fields (_linux_fd, _resolved_path) — must not change public struct size
- Missing type headers: builtins.h, unixlib.h, VMS-extended signal.h/errno.h/stat.h

Validation: Eight-Cubed stdio programs work. Simpler MMK files begin to compile.

Subsumes vms-iuu.

title: Milestone 2: MMK compiles, links, and processes an MMS file
description:
Deliverable: MMK (MadGoat Make, 57 C files, BSD-3-Clause) compiles against OVMX headers, links against OVMX libraries, and successfully processes a simple MMS description file to build a target.

MMK exercises APIs well beyond simple examples:
- CLI$ command-line processing (cli$present, cli$get_value, cli$dcl_parse)
- LIB$TPARSE state-table parser
- lib$find_file / lib$find_file_end (wildcard file search)
- sys$parse / sys$search (RMS file parsing)
- lib$spawn (subprocess execution)
- lib$get_foreign (foreign command line)
- sys$filescan (lightweight filespec parsing)

This milestone proves Tier 2 compatibility: CLI framework, table-driven parsing, wildcard operations, subprocess control.

Process:
1. Run harness against tier3-mmk corpus
2. Triage compile failures
3. Implement missing CLI$ routines, lib$tparse, sys$filescan
4. Iterate until MMK links
5. Run MMK against a test MMS file
6. Milestone done when MMK processes the file correctly

Subsumes vms-cbp.

title: Milestone 3: NETLIB compiles — QIO + AST networking proven
description:
Deliverable: NETLIB (endlesssoftware/netlib, BSD-3-Clause) compiles against OVMX headers and links against OVMX libraries.

NETLIB is the clearest example of VMS-style async QIO-based networking in C:
- sys$qiow (foundation of all VMS I/O)
- AST callbacks (asynchronous system traps)
- sys$assign / sys$dassgn (device assignment)
- DNS system services
- UCX/MultiNet/TCPware device I/O paths

If NETLIB compiles and links cleanly, it proves QIO + AST + device assignment work — which is the foundation for any VMS server application.

Stretch: After NETLIB, attempt MX (email server, 20-50k LOC) or a WASD subset. These prove the full VMS application stack.

This milestone proves Tier 3 compatibility: async I/O, networking, the complete VMS I/O model.

title: DCL: DEFINE/USER_MODE I/O redirection (Phase 1)
description:
Implement I/O redirection via DEFINE/USER_MODE SYS$OUTPUT and SYS$INPUT.

Context hint: Systems

Scope:
- Add dcl_io_override_t struct to dcl_context_t (context.h)
- Modify cmd_define() in dcl_builtin.c to detect /USER_MODE qualifier and set override struct
- Modify dcl_execute_line() / command dispatch in dcl_exec.c to fork a child when override is set, apply dup2() for redirected FDs, execute in child, clear override after
- Update dcl_read_input() and dcl_write_output() in dcl_io.c to consult override
- Support SYS$OUTPUT, SYS$INPUT, SYS$ERROR redirects
- User-mode = one-shot: override clears after the next command

Done condition: DEFINE/USER_MODE SYS$OUTPUT file.txt followed by a command writes to file.txt, not stdout. Verified by running DCL and inspecting file contents.

Design: docs/design-dcl-pipes.md

title: DCL: PIPE command with | operator (Phase 2)
description:
Implement PIPE command supporting single-stage pipes: PIPE cmd1 | cmd2 | cmd3.

Context hint: Systems

Scope:
- Replace cmd_pipe() stub in dcl_builtin.c with real implementation
- Parse PIPE argument string on | boundaries to extract per-stage DCL commands
- For each | segment: fork() + dup2() to connect pipe FDs (Unix pipe(2) as conduit)
- Execute each DCL command segment in a child subprocess
- Wait for all children; propagate last child exit status to $STATUS
- Support pipelines of 2+ stages
- Define SYS$PIPE logical in child context pointing to stdin (for SEARCH SYS$PIPE etc.)

Done condition: PIPE TYPE foo.txt | SEARCH SYS$PIPE "pattern" works correctly. Output of first command flows to input of second. Verified by integration test.

Design: docs/design-dcl-pipes.md
Blocked by: vms-802 (Phase 1 — I/O redirection must land first so override infrastructure exists)

title: DCL: PIPE compound operators && || ; (Phase 3)
description:
Extend PIPE command to support compound operators: &&, ||, ;

Context hint: Systems

Scope:
- Extend the PIPE command argument parser to tokenize && || ; in addition to |
- Build a sequential dispatch loop for compound PIPE (not just fork-and-pipe)
- Implement VMS conditional semantics: odd status = success for &&; even status = success for ||; ; always runs next
- Compound operators and | may be mixed: PIPE cmd1 | cmd2 && cmd3
- Propagate $STATUS from last executed command

Done condition: All three operators work with correct conditional behavior. Verified by integration tests. PIPE cmd1 && cmd2: cmd2 only runs when cmd1 succeeds (odd $STATUS). PIPE cmd1 || cmd2: cmd2 only runs when cmd1 fails (even $STATUS).

Design: docs/design-dcl-pipes.md
Blocked by: vms-803 (Phase 2 — pipe | operator must exist first)

title: DCL: pipes and redirection integration tests (Phase 4)
description:
Write integration tests for all pipe and I/O redirection scenarios.

Context hint: QA

Scope:
- Add test cases to tests/integration/ covering:
  - DEFINE/USER_MODE SYS$OUTPUT to file: verify file contents
  - DEFINE/USER_MODE SYS$INPUT from file: verify command reads from file
  - PIPE cmd | cmd two-stage: stdout flows correctly
  - PIPE cmd | cmd | cmd three-stage pipeline
  - PIPE cmd && cmd: second runs only on success
  - PIPE cmd || cmd: second runs only on failure
  - PIPE cmd ; cmd: second always runs
  - Error conditions: bad redirect file, failed pipe stage
- Update CMakeLists.txt to include new test programs
- Verify CI passes end-to-end after all phases

Done condition: All test cases pass. CI green. No regressions in existing integration tests.

Design: docs/design-dcl-pipes.md
Blocked by: vms-804 (Phase 3 — all implementation must be complete before full test coverage)

title: Provide errchk.h compatibility header for Eight-Cubed corpus
description:
Deliverable: tests/corpus/tier1-examples/errchk.h compatibility header.

The Eight-Cubed examples all #include "errchk.h" which provides error-checking macros. This header is NOT a VMS system header — it is part of the Eight-Cubed example suite. It was not included in the corpus download.

Required macros (extracted from usage):
- errchk_sig(status) — if status is error, call lib$signal(status)
- errchk_ret(status) — if status is error, return status
- errchk_abort(status) — if status is error, abort
- errchk_stop(status) — if status is error, call lib$stop(status)

All use $VMS_STATUS_SUCCESS() from stsdef.h to test the status.

Impact: Unblocks 81 programs (35% of corpus) that have NO other missing dependencies.

title: Fix: enable_testing() must precede add_subdirectory() in top-level CMakeLists.txt
description:
BUG: ctest reports 'No tests were found!!' even though 7 libvmssys test executables are built.

Root cause: In CMakeLists.txt, enable_testing() is called on line 73 AFTER all add_subdirectory() calls (lines 59-70). CMake processes add_test() calls in subdirectories correctly when enable_testing() appears before those subdirectory includes, but the CTest test database is only populated correctly when enable_testing() appears at the right scope level.

Result: cmake --build works, test binaries are produced, but 'ctest' finds 0 tests.

Fix: Move enable_testing() call to before the first add_subdirectory() call (before line 59).

File: /vms/CMakeLists.txt

Deliverable: All 7 libvmssys tests appear in 'ctest -N' output and pass in 'ctest --output-on-failure'.
